title: Extracting the physical content of Liouvillian eigenmodes: Semiclassical quantization
authors: Ashlin V Thomas, Felix Fritzsch, Masudul Haque, Shovan Dutta
abstract: Unlike in closed quantum systems where individual energy eigenstates are understood as physical excitations, open quantum systems have distinct right and left eigenstates of the Liouvillian that decay with time and are difficult to interpret. Here we introduce a physically motivated quasiprobability measure combining the two types of eigenstates that interprets a Liouville eigenmode as a set of coherences. This coherence measure is intimately connected to the return probability and allows one to visualize the modes as quasiprobability distributions in a "doubled" phase space. Using this measure we show that, remarkably, an oscillator retains its quantized "orbits" in phase space for a large class of linear and nonlinear damping, thus providing a formulation of semiclassical quantization for open systems. The orbits have measurable dynamical signatures and are broadened in the presence of a thermal bath, similar to energy levels. For quadratic systems, our results yield an extension of the concept of invariant tori, which play a central role in Hamiltonian systems.
summary: The paper develops a novel quasiprobability measure to give physical meaning to Liouvillian eigenmodes in open quantum systems. By interpreting these modes as coherence distributions, the authors successfully generalize semiclassical quantization concepts, showing that quantized orbital structures persist even under damping from a thermal bath.
main_problem: The primary challenge is interpreting the physical meaning of Liouvillian eigenmodes for open quantum systems, where standard energy eigenstates are insufficient due to time-decaying right and left eigenstates.
main_result: The authors introduce a quasiprobability measure that successfully interprets an eigenmode as a coherence distribution, demonstrating that semiclassical quantization concepts (like quantized orbits) can be extended to dissipative open systems.
method: They employ a physically motivated quasiprobability measure combining right and left eigenstates, mapping the dynamics onto a doubled phase space structure. This allows for analyzing spectral properties via generalized Husimi functions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum systems governed by Lindblad master equations ($ rac{d\hat{ho}}{dt} = L\hat{ho}$), specifically modeling damped harmonic oscillators and quadratic Liouvillians. The analysis uses Fock basis representations and superoperators.
key_observables: Coherence measure ($C_p$), return probability, Super Husimi function $C_{n_K, n_B}(\alpha_K, \alpha_B)$, and the persistence of quantized 'orbits' in phase space.
important_parameters: Damping rates ($\gamma$), thermal bath temperature (related to $ eta$), and relative phases ($\phi$) between coherent components.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are assumed to be CPTP (Completely Positive Trace-Preserving) and Markovian. For quantization results, the damping is often assumed isotropic in phase space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quantized 'orbits' for damped oscillators, show the Liouville spectrum revealing coherence between Fock states, and map out sections of the super Husimi function in doubled phase space, demonstrating peak locations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for a new measure (quasiprobability) to interpret open system dynamics. It then applies this framework to simple models like the damped oscillator, deriving explicit formulas and asymptotic results for coherence distributions and return amplitudes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—the quasiprobability measure—to bridge semiclassical quantization concepts (like invariant tori) from conservative Hamiltonian systems into the complex realm of open quantum dynamics governed by dissipation.
